steps.body: Time intervals work the same way: five shifts of 30 minutes is 150 minutes, and finishing 20 minutes early leaves 130.
steps.narration: Time intervals work the same way: five shifts of 30 minutes is 150 minutes, and finishing 20 minutes early leaves 130.

widget.prompt: Five shifts of 30 minutes — hop one shift at a time.

commonLandings.feedback: Four hops reach 120 minutes; there are five shifts.
Six hops overshoot — five shifts of 30 minutes is 150.

widget.missFeedback: Each shift is 30 minutes, so five reach 150.
widget.successFeedback: 150 minutes — five shift-hops of 30 minutes each, which is two and a half hours.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — each shift is 30 minutes, so five reach 150.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — five shifts of 30 minutes stops exactly at 150.

predict.prompt: Five 30-minute shifts, answer wanted in hours. Which moment to convert keeps the work cleaner?
predict.reveal: Either way lands on the same two and a half hours here; one conversion at the end is simply cleaner than five, and avoids fractions before they are needed.

cml.actionGoal: Build a time total from equal shifts, adjust it once, and convert only if requested.
invariants: Equal shifts multiply; finishing early subtracts once from the total.
misconceptions: Adding the shift count to the minutes per shift.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the unit got ten times smaller, what would happen to the number that measures the same object?

widget.prompt: A trail crew works 4 shifts of 45 minutes and finishes 13 minutes early. How many minutes?

commonErrors.feedback: That is the planned time; the crew finished 13 minutes before it was used up.
Adding a shift count to a shift length mixes two different quantities — 4 shifts OF 45 minutes multiply.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Multiply to build the equal-group total, then subtract the one stated adjustment.

widget.prompt: Model a second interval: four shifts of 45 minutes. Hop one shift at a time.

commonLandings.feedback: Three hops represent three shifts; four shifts needs one more hop.
Five hops overshoot; four shifts total 180 minutes.

widget.missFeedback: Four equal hops of 45 minutes land at 180 minutes.
widget.successFeedback: 180 minutes — four shift-hops of 45 minutes each.
widget.lowFeedback: This landing is short of four complete shifts.
widget.highFeedback: This landing is past four complete shifts.

widget.prompt: Apply without the opening model: "A crew works 5 shifts of 30 minutes, then converts the total to hours." What is the correct ORDER?

options.label: Multiply to find 150 minutes, then divide by 60
options.feedback: Correct — build the total in one unit first, then convert it once; 150 minutes is 2.5 hours.

options.label: Divide 30 by 60 first, then multiply by 5
options.feedback: It reaches the same value, but converting each shift first invites fractions before they are needed.

options.label: Add 5 and 30, then divide by 60
options.feedback: Adding a shift count to a shift length mixes quantities; 5 shifts OF 30 minutes multiply.

options.label: Multiply 150 by 60
options.feedback: Hours are BIGGER than minutes, so the number must shrink — that means dividing.

widget.prompt: Retrieve or diagnose in a new form: A hike measures 360 minutes, and each hour is 60 minutes. Compute 360 ÷ 60.

commonErrors.feedback: 360 is the count in minutes. Switching to the bigger hour must make the NUMBER smaller.
That multiplied. Going to the BIGGER unit needs fewer of them, so divide.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Name the quantity and the conversion factor, then decide whether the count should grow or shrink.
